proposed.explanation: Approving the routing without verification of its impact on other systems repeats the clash detection and resolution process during construction, defeating the purpose of design-phase coordination. While combined services drawings are binding, a contractor may identify more efficient routing if properly coordinated with other trades. The architect should review the proposal's merit before rejecting it. Allowing conflicts to reach punch lists increases change orders, schedule delays, and coordination overhead during construction. Shop drawing review is the architect's opportunity to catch conflicts before installation begins. Shop drawings are construction-phase documents that must align with the design-phase coordination decisions documented in combined services drawings. When a contractor proposes routing that differs from combined services drawings, the architect must verify the proposal doesn't create new conflicts. A coordination review between affected contractors ensures the revised routing satisfies all system requirements. Shop drawing review is a critical coordination checkpoint. The architect must verify that any deviations from combined services drawings don't create new conflicts. When conflicts are identified, a brief coordination review is faster and cheaper than resolving them during construction.
